assumptions.text: Added `--with jsonschema --with markdown` to the `task` and `suite` commands, because scripts run under the test Python no longer get their inline dependencies from `uv run`.
Left the `uv run` calls in tests other than `conftest.py` (`test_build.py`, `test_lesson_curation.py`, `test_repo_memory.py`), because E3 and S3 only name `conftest.py` and the fake adapter.
Per-example results are read from pytest -rA output lines (PASSED/FAILED/ERROR ... test_eN_). The task command in harness.toml now includes -rA; other stacks must print the same line shape.
red_exit is no longer consulted in T0; an example is red if the runner prints a FAILED/ERROR line for it.
No test shares a fixed path or port: they use tmp_path and bind no ports. The parallel run showed no collisions, so I made no isolation changes.
E1 and E2 fail because the suite timing, the page and the budget check do not exist yet. They belong to a later task, not T3.
Test time is the sum of `run_raw` durations (the task check) in one build process. It is kept in a module-level `TEST_TIME` in build.py. It includes the T0 run and every retry.
If `limits.suite_seconds` is absent, accept does not check the budget. Other adopters' configs stay valid.
tests/conftest.py strips `suite_seconds = 30` from the copied slice config. The frozen E2 test inserts its own `suite_seconds` line into `[limits]`, and a duplicate key makes the TOML invalid.
Accept writes `suite_seconds` into the in-memory report, so it is also saved in build-report.json when accept escalates. It is not in the saved `runs` entries.
Cause inferred from the code (same-size rewrite within one second reusing a stale .pyc); the flake was not reproduced before the fix, so the fix is not shown to cure an observed failure.
Fixed in build.py revert() rather than only in test fixtures, because real builds hit the same stale-bytecode path.

escalations.reason: S6 (the commit message of e044ca1) can only be fixed by amending history, which is outside what I may do, so I left it for the owner or build script.

S6: R1: the commit message does not name the root cause. Commit e044ca1 says only 'build(035-fast-tests): T5 remove the root cause of the flaky revert test', which repeats the task title and has no body. The cause appears only in a code comment in scripts/build.py revert(): a reverted source rewritten in the same second with the same size reuses its stale __pycache__ .pyc. The commit message must state that cause. (The other part of R1 is met: the diff adds no sleep, retry or skip.)
